Operating Characteristics of the BF-BOIN-ET Design

Source: R/sim_bf_boin_et.R
sim_bf_boin_et.Rd

Simulate trials of the backfill BOIN-ET (BF-BOIN-ET) design of Takeda, Zhu and Hirakawa (2025) under one scenario of DLT and response probabilities, select the optimal biological dose (OBD) of each trial, and summarize how often each dose is selected, how many patients are treated and backfilled at each dose, and how long the trials last.

Usage

sim_bf_boin_et(
  target,
  target_resp,
  p_true,
  p_resp,
  n_cohort,
  cohort_size,
  window,
  accrual_rate,
  resp_window = window,
  accrual = c("uniform", "exponential", "fixed"),
  event_time = c("weibull", "uniform"),
  late_fraction = 0.5,
  resp_late_fraction = 0.5,
  resp_cor = 0.2,
  n_trials = 10000,
  start_dose = 1,
  n_earlystop = 12,
  n_elimination = 6,
  suspend = 0,
  p_saf = NULL,
  p_tox = NULL,
  p_saf_resp = NULL,
  cutoff_eli = 0.95,
  cutoff_eli_resp = 0.9,
  psi00 = 40,
  psi11 = 60,
  psi_resp_no_dlt = 100,
  psi_dlt_no_resp = 0,
  backfill_extension = 100,
  keep_trials = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  seed = 123
)

Arguments

target

Numeric scalar. Target DLT probability.

target_resp

Numeric scalar. Lowest response probability of interest. A dose is excluded when its response rate is likely below it, and the backfill doses start from the lowest dose whose response rate reaches the boundary eta1 derived from it.

p_true

Numeric vector. True DLT probability at each dose level, in increasing dose order.

p_resp

Numeric vector of the same length as p_true. True response probability at each dose level.

n_cohort

Integer scalar. Number of cohorts in a trial.

cohort_size

Integer scalar or vector. Number of patients per cohort. A scalar is used for every cohort. A vector shorter than n_cohort is padded with its last element and a longer one is truncated.

window

Numeric scalar. Length of the DLT assessment window.

accrual_rate

Numeric scalar. Average number of patients arriving per unit of time, in the same unit as window. The accrual argument of the 'boinet' package is the average time between arrivals, its inverse.

resp_window

Numeric scalar. Length of the response assessment window. Defaults to window.

accrual

Character scalar. Distribution of the times between arrivals: "uniform" (the default, as in 'boinet') on (0, 2 / accrual_rate), "exponential" for a Poisson process, or "fixed" for arrivals exactly 1 / accrual_rate apart.

event_time

Character scalar. Distribution of the times to DLT and to response: "weibull" (the default), with the share of the events in the second half of the window set by late_fraction and resp_late_fraction, or "uniform" on (0, window / p) for an event of probability p. With "weibull" the probabilities must be below 1.

late_fraction

Numeric scalar strictly between 0 and 1. Share of the DLTs that occur in the second half of the DLT window under the Weibull distribution. Defaults to 0.5.

resp_late_fraction

Numeric scalar strictly between 0 and 1. The same for the responses. Defaults to 0.5.

resp_cor

Numeric scalar strictly between -1 and 1. Correlation of the Gaussian copula that links the time to DLT and the time to response of a patient. Defaults to 0.2, the default of the 'boinet' package.

n_trials

Integer scalar. Number of trials to simulate. Defaults to 10000.

start_dose

Integer scalar. Dose level for the first cohort. Defaults to 1.

n_earlystop

Integer scalar. Number of patients at a dose, dose escalation and backfill together, that closes it to backfilling, and that ends the trial when it is reached at the current dose and the decision would keep the trial there. Defaults to 12, the default of the 'bfboinet' package.

n_elimination

Integer scalar. Number of patients a dose needs before it can be excluded. Defaults to 6.

suspend

Numeric scalar from 0 to 1. Share of the patients at the current dose whose DLT assessment may still be running when the next cohort starts. Defaults to 0, which waits until the DLT outcomes of the cohort are known.

p_saf

Numeric scalar or NULL. Highest DLT probability deemed subtherapeutic, used for the escalation boundary. Defaults to 0.6 * target.

p_tox

Numeric scalar or NULL. Lowest DLT probability deemed overly toxic, used for the de-escalation boundary. Defaults to 1.4 * target.

p_saf_resp

Numeric scalar or NULL. Response probability deemed subtherapeutic, used for the response boundary. Defaults to 0.6 * target_resp.

cutoff_eli

Numeric scalar. A dose with n_elimination patients or more is excluded, together with every higher dose, when the posterior probability that its DLT rate exceeds target is above this cutoff. Defaults to 0.95.

cutoff_eli_resp

Numeric scalar. Such a dose is excluded alone when the posterior probability that its response rate is below target_resp is above this cutoff. Defaults to 0.90.

psi00, psi11

Numeric scalars. Scores of a patient without DLT or response and of a patient with both, which define, with psi_resp_no_dlt and psi_dlt_no_resp, the utility used to choose the backfill dose and the OBD. Default to 40 and 60.

psi_resp_no_dlt, psi_dlt_no_resp

Numeric scalars. Scores of a patient with a response and no DLT and of a patient with a DLT and no response. Default to 100 and 0. The 'bfboinet' package calls them ppsi10 and ppsi01.

backfill_extension

Numeric scalar. Time, in the unit of window, during which backfilling continues after the last cohort has been enrolled. Defaults to 100, the value fixed in the 'bfboinet' package.

keep_trials

Logical scalar. Keep the simulated trials and the selected OBDs in the result. Defaults to FALSE.

verbose

Logical scalar. Report progress with messages. Defaults to FALSE.

seed

Integer scalar or NULL. Random seed. When NULL the current state of the random number generator is used. The state of the calling session is restored on exit. Defaults to 123.

Value

An object of class bf_boin_et_oc, which is a list with components

design

"BF-BOIN-ET".

target, target_resp, p_true, p_resp

The targets and the scenario.

n_doses, n_trials

Numbers of doses and of simulated trials.

lambda1, lambda2, eta1

The escalation and de-escalation boundaries of the DLT rate and the boundary of the response rate.

sel_percent

Percentage of trials selecting each dose as the OBD.

percent_no_obd

Percentage of trials selecting no OBD.

percent_early_stop

Percentage of trials stopped because every dose was excluded.

n_pts_dose, n_bf_dose

Average numbers of patients treated and of patients backfilled at each dose.

n_tox_dose, n_resp_dose

Average numbers of DLTs and responses at each dose observed at the last decision.

n_tox_bf_dose, n_resp_bf_dose

The same among the backfilled patients.

total_n_pts, total_n_bf, total_n_tox, total_n_resp

Their averages per trial.

duration

Average time until the last patient finishes both assessments.

stop_reason_percent

Percentage of trials ending for each reason, see Details.

settings

List of the design parameters.

call

The matched call.

trials

When keep_trials is TRUE, a list with the matrices n_pts, n_bf, n_tox, n_resp, n_tox_bf and n_resp_bf (one row per trial), and the vectors cohorts_used, stop_reason, early_stop, obd (NA when none) and duration.

Details

The rules are those of bfboinet::get.oc.backboinet() (version 1.1.0). A cohort is treated at the current dose. The next cohort starts with the first patient who arrives once the DLT outcomes of the cohort are known (or, with suspend, once enough of them are), and after the last cohort backfilling goes on for backfill_extension. The patients who arrive in between are backfilled one by one, when the current dose is not the lowest, to the backfill dose with the highest utility (ties to the higher dose), the DLT rates being made monotone by isotonic regression; doses with n_earlystop patients take no more.

The decision uses the DLT rate at the current dose, which counts a patient still under assessment by the fraction of the window followed, with the boundaries lambda1 and lambda2 of BOIN; after 1 DLT in 3 patients the trial stays. The backfill doses for the next cohort are the admissible doses from the lowest dose whose response rate is at least eta1 up to the current dose (escalation), the dose below it (stay) or two doses below it (de-escalation). Once excluded, a dose stays excluded, and an escalation moves past a dose excluded by its response data only. The OBD is the admissible dose up to the estimated MTD with the highest utility, from the observed rates at the last decision; ties go to the lower dose.

Possible values of stop_reason are "no_admissible_dose" (the only early stop, which selects no OBD when fewer patients than the maximum sample size have been treated), "lowest_dose_excluded", "top_dose_excluded", "no_lower_admissible_dose", "n_earlystop" and "max_cohorts".

The 'bfboinet' package reports the position of the OBD among the doses tried, which is the dose itself when the trial starts at the lowest dose; the dose is reported here in every case.

References

Takeda, K., Zhu, J. and Hirakawa, A. (2025). BF-BOIN-ET: A backfill Bayesian optimal interval design using efficacy and toxicity outcomes for dose optimization. Pharmaceutical Statistics, 24, e2470. doi:10.1002/pst.2470

See also

sim_bf_boin_et_multi, sim_tite_boin_et

Examples

# The example of bfboinet::get.oc.backboinet(): windows of one month and
# three patients a month
oc <- sim_bf_boin_et(
  target = 0.30, target_resp = 0.25,
  p_true = c(0.03, 0.05, 0.20, 0.22, 0.45),
  p_resp = c(0.05, 0.10, 0.50, 0.68, 0.70),
  n_cohort = 10, cohort_size = 3, window = 1, accrual_rate = 3,
  n_trials = 300, seed = 123
)
oc
#> BF-BOIN-ET operating characteristics
#>   target DLT rate      : 0.3
#>   target response rate : 0.25
#>   trials               : 300
#>   cohorts              : 10 of size 3
#>   patients per dose    : 12 at most with backfill
#>   lambda1 / lambda2    : 0.2365 / 0.3585
#>   eta1                 : 0.1968
#> 
#>                        DL1  DL2  DL3  DL4  DL5 Total / No OBD
#> True DLT rate (%)      3.0  5.0 20.0 22.0 45.0               
#> True response rate (%) 5.0 10.0 50.0 68.0 70.0               
#> OBD selected (%)       3.0  2.7 41.0 48.7  4.7            0.0
#> Patients treated       4.1  6.0 11.4  9.5  5.0           36.1
#> Patients backfilled    0.7  1.5  4.5  2.5  0.1            9.4
#> Patients with DLT      0.1  0.3  2.3  2.0  2.4            7.1
#> Patients with response 0.2  0.6  5.7  6.5  3.6           16.6
#> 
#> Trials stopped early: 0%
#> Average trial duration: 16.6
